'''Martin Maximilian Emil Eichler''' (29 March 1912 &ndash; 7 October 1992) was a German [[mathematics|mathematician]].

Eichler received his Ph.D. from the [[Martin Luther University]] of Halle-Wittenberg in 1936.

Eichler and [[Goro Shimura]] developed a method to construct [[elliptic curve]]s from certain [[modular forms]].  The [[modularity theorem|converse notion]] that every elliptic curve has a corresponding modular form would later be the key to the proof of [[Fermat's Last Theorem]].<ref>{{cite web  | url=https://www.ias.edu/about/publications/ias-letter/articles/2012-summer/modular-arithmetic-taylor  | title=Modular Arithmetic: Driven by Inherent Beauty and Human Curiosity | work=Institute for Advanced Study
 | author=Richard Taylor
 | date=2012
 | access-date=2014-12-22 }}
</ref><ref>{{cite book|isbn=978-0465050741|title=Love and Math: The Heart of Hidden Reality|url=https://archive.org/details/lovemathheartofh0000fren|url-access=registration|author=Edward Frenkel|author-link=Edward Frenkel|pages=[https://archive.org/details/lovemathheartofh0000fren/page/90 90]}}</ref>
